intro: Lesson 27: The particle model. To understand how the arrangement and movement of particles explains the properties of each state

picture.find: particle model solid liquid gas diagram
picture.alt: Particle diagrams of a solid, a liquid and a gas
picture.draw: Draw and label: Particle diagram sheet

questions.q: Use the particle model to explain why a solid keeps its shape.
questions.a: Particles are held in fixed positions by strong forces and only vibrate.
questions.model: Arrangement: regular, touching. Movement: vibrate on the spot. Forces: strong. So the particles cannot move around and the shape stays fixed.

questions.q: Draw 9 particles of a gas in a box (describe your drawing).
questions.a: Particles spread out, far apart, randomly placed, with arrows in different directions.

questions.q: Do particles get bigger when a solid melts?
questions.a: No: they move more and change arrangement; they stay the same size.

questions.q: Core: Draw labelled particle diagrams of ice, water and steam, each with two sentences about arrangement and movement.
questions.a: Ice: regular, touching, vibrating; water: random, touching, sliding; steam: far apart, fast, random.
questions.model: Teacher draws ice first: a 4 by 4 grid of touching circles, small wiggle marks: 'regular pattern, particles vibrate'.

questions.q: Extend: Use the model to explain why gases can be compressed but liquids cannot.
questions.a: Gas particles have big spaces between them; liquid particles are already touching.

questions.q: Stretch: Give one limitation of drawing particles as circles.
questions.a: Real particles are not solid balls; diagrams are 2D and do not show movement or forces well.

questions.q: Big question: what would you see if you zoomed in on ice, water and steam?
questions.a: The same water particles: regular and vibrating in ice, touching and sliding in water, far apart and fast in steam.
